title: The circular's conditions for dispensing by administration and prescriber reassessment
rule_summary: Circular Letter DCP 26-03-124 (March 11, 2026) provides that a pharmacist or a pharmacy intern may, without obtaining a Massachusetts Controlled Substance Registration (MCSR), dispense by administration (i.e. administer) FDA-approved drugs included in its list of Medications Eligible for Pharmacist or Pharmacy Intern Administration to persons 18 years or older, provided that: (a) the pharmacist or pharmacy intern is authorized to dispense controlled substances, in accordance with M.G.L. c. 112; (b) administration is conducted pursuant to a valid prescription; (c) administration is not intravenous; (d) the medication is available in single-dose packaging and prescribed in single doses, with or without refills; (e) the prescription is subject to reassessment by the prescriber at appropriate intervals, as determined by the prescriber, if applicable; and (f) the activity is conducted in accordance with Department guidelines. Under Prescriber Assessment, prescribers must regularly re-assess the patient and prescription at appropriate intervals, such as quarterly, to be determined by the prescriber; this assessment does not preclude the issuance of valid prescriptions with available refills; and if a pharmacist or pharmacy intern is presented with a prescription and has questions about the interval transpiring between assessments, routine communication with the prescriber is encouraged, but not required, prior to administration.
exam_relevance: Tests the full set of conditions a pharmacist or intern relies on when administering under the circular: no MCSR is needed but authority to dispense controlled substances is, the person treated must be 18 years or older, administration runs on a valid prescription, and prescriber reassessment neither rules out refills nor requires contact with the prescriber before administration.

authority.name: Circular Letter DCP 26-03-124, Pharmacist Administration of Medications, March 11, 2026

numeric_facts.fact: minimum age of persons to whom eligible medications may be administered
numeric_facts.conditions: persons 18 years or older, under the circular's Dispensing by Administration

numeric_facts.fact: example of an appropriate reassessment interval
numeric_facts.conditions: given as an example; the interval is to be determined by the prescriber

exceptions: Routine communication with the prescriber about the interval between assessments is encouraged, but not required, prior to administration.
Prescriber reassessment does not preclude the issuance of valid prescriptions with available refills.
common_confusions: Treating quarterly as a fixed reassessment deadline rather than the circular's example of an interval the prescriber determines.
Assuming the pharmacist must contact the prescriber about reassessment before administering.
Reading administration without an MCSR as removing the condition that the pharmacist or pharmacy intern be authorized to dispense controlled substances in accordance with M.G.L. c. 112.
verification_notes: Read on 2026-09-14 in Circular Letter DCP 26-03-124, Pharmacist Administration of Medications, dated March 11, 2026, in the Word document linked from the Department's news page on mass.gov.
